<!--
Developing this vignette:

1. Load your in-development code, not an installed copy:
     devtools::load_all()
2. Preview/knit against that dev-loaded code in the SAME R session:
     rmarkdown::render("vignettes/reproduce-mobility-ms.Rmd", output_dir = tempdir())
   (output_dir = tempdir() keeps the rendered .html out of this directory,
   so you don't accidentally commit it -- the knitr cache still lands in
   vignettes/reproduce-mobility-ms_cache/, which is the point, see #4.)
   devtools::build_rmd()/build_vignettes() are both deprecated AND wrong
   for this: they knit in an isolated callr subprocess that does NOT
   inherit load_all()'s state (confirmed empirically -- it fails with
   "could not find function ..." for any package function). A bare
   library(fluscapeR) call, or hitting an IDE's Knit button directly, has
   the same problem from a different cause: it uses the last *installed*
   version and silently ignores your edits -- some IDEs (confirmed for
   RStudio; untested for VS Code) spawn a fresh R session for Knit, which
   never saw your load_all() call either.
3. Working directory: knitr runs this file's chunks with the working
   directory set to vignettes/, not the package root -- use system.file()
   or package data (as load_gz_pop_raster() does below), not relative
   paths, to avoid chunks that only work from one invocation method.
4. The table1-pure-gravity chunk below is cache = TRUE (see
   reproduce-mobility-ms_cache/, gitignored) because the fit takes several
   minutes. Delete that directory, or call knitr::clean_cache(), to force
   a fresh run -- do this before any build you intend to ship or commit.
-->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

## Table 1: pure gravity

<!-- TODO: prose explaining the pure-gravity model (one free parameter, no
offset, no destination power) and pointing out this is only one of six
model rows in the published table. -->

`noRepeats` is set to 1 below to keep this vignette's build time
reasonable; increase it for a more rigorous multi-start fit. This chunk is
cached (see `vignettes/reproduce-mobility-ms_cache/`, gitignored) since the
fit takes several minutes -- delete the cache directory (or
`knitr::clean_cache()`) to force a fresh run, e.g. before a build you
intend to ship or commit.

```{r table1-pure-gravity, cache = TRUE}
knitr::kable(
  table1_pure_gravity(contacts_V1_jittered_100m, load_gz_pop_raster(), noRepeats = 1)
)
```

## Figure 8: the S matrix for the radiation model

<!-- TODO: prose explaining what the S matrix represents (population
within distance r_ij of each origin cell, per Figure 8's published
caption/algorithm) and why the demo below uses an aggregated raster rather
than the full-resolution one the published figure's S matrix was actually
built from. -->

`generate.agg.Smatrix()` optionally aggregates the population raster
before computing the S matrix (`agg_num` cells merged into one), trading
resolution for speed. At full resolution (`agg_num = 0`) this is still on
the order of minutes even with the vectorized implementation used below
(`vectorized = TRUE`) -- see `?generate.agg.Smatrix`. This chunk uses
`agg_num = 10` to stay fast; increase/zero it to build the matrix actually
used for model fitting.

```{r s-matrix, cache = TRUE}
s_demo <- generate.agg.Smatrix(
  contacts_V1_jittered_100m, load_gz_pop_raster(),
  agg_num = 10, vectorized = TRUE
)
dim(s_demo$S)
```
